title: Incremental model admission protocol: policy DSL for phased rollouts, shadowing and auto-rollback
creator: Priya Patel
description: Design and implement a policy-driven Incremental Model Admission Protocol (IMAP) that unifies traffic splitting, phased schedules, shadow routing, A/B cohorting and automated rollback actions. The goal is a declarative DSL + controller that lets platform teams define safe, metric-driven rollouts for new model versions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments. IMAP should support time- or metric-driven steps, guardrail expressions, shadow probes (non-allocating mirrors), and automated remediation (throttle/rollback/fallback).
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL: authors can express a rollout as a list of steps with either explicit traffic percentages or metric predicates (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%)
Shadowing: configuration supports 0-cost shadow probes that mirror a configurable % of traffic asynchronously for quality checks without impacting user path
Metric guardrails: support semantic-quality, error-rate and latency predicates; controller halts progression and triggers rollback if predicates breach thresholds
A/B cohorting: policies can target cohorts by header, cookie, or random sampling seed; SDK and proxy honor cohort selection deterministically
Auto-rollback: automated rollback action (rollback to pinned model or route to fallback variant) fires when a severity rule is tripped and creates an audit event
Observability: rollout events (step start/end/failures), decision rationale, and per-step telemetry are emitted and visible in Console release dashboard
Backward compatibility: current rollout API remains operational; IMAP exposes a compatibility layer that maps existing simple traffic-split configs into the DSL
E2E tests: integration tests cover policy parsing, scheduling, metric-evaluator and rollback flow including shadow probes in staging environment
design_notes: We will implement a small expressive DSL (YAML/JSON) that describes steps, selectors, guardrails and actions. Example step: {duration: 30m, traffic: 5%, guardrails: [latency_p95 < 250ms, error_rate_delta < 0.5%], on_failure: rollback}

Prefer controller-based evaluation (centralized decision engine) over distributed per-node logic to simplify consistent rollback and audit trails. Controller will signal routers via configuration snapshots + atomic versioned API.

Shadow traffic should be handled by the request proxy: clone request and send to candidate model path asynchronously; drop or store outputs based on policy for offline evaluation. Avoid introducing latency in the hot path.

Quality guardrails should support both absolute thresholds and delta-based comparisons vs baseline model. Allow weighting of evaluation datasets and multiple signal sources (synthetic probes + live user probes).
Security: sensitive request payloads subject to sampling/filtering for shadowing in Private/VPC deployments; KMS/HSM keys used for audit logs where required.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 sprints): Define DSL schema + parser, controller scaffolding, policy storage in metadata DB; implement compatibility adapter for existing simple splits
Phase 2 (2 sprints): Router snapshot API, proxy shadowing hooks, cohort selector integration in SDKs, initial guardrail metric evaluator (latency/error-rate)
Phase 3 (1 sprint): Auto-rollback executor, audit/event plumbing to Console, rollout UI prototypes and telemetry dashboards
Phase 4 (1 sprint): Extend guardrails with semantic-quality signals (eval harness integration), stress tests on Dedicated clusters, enterprise security review and docs
rollout_plan: Beta: internal teams only (small subset of org) with shadowing and manual step advancement
Staged: enable automated steps and rollback in Hosted non-critical namespaces with monitoring for two weeks
GA: enable full features and Console UI, announce to customers with migration guide and deprecation timeline for old rollout APIs
telemetry_and_alerting: Emit per-policy metrics: policy_version, step_index, step_start_ts, step_end_ts, traffic_percent, guardrail_eval_count
Guardrail alerts: fire when (error_rate_candidate - error_rate_baseline) > 0.75% for 5m aggregated at 1m granularity
Latency alert: p95_candidate > p95_baseline + 200ms sustained for 3 consecutive 1m windows
Semantic quality regression: if eval_set_score drops > 1.5 points vs baseline over 200 samples, generate P1 incident and auto-pause the rollout
Audit log: every automated action (advance/pause/rollback) creates immutable event with rationale and pointers to telemetry snapshots
